scope: Live macOS iTerm2 check on a private tmux socket with disposable /bin/cat panes

product_lifecycle.cleanup: detached the exact viewer clients and killed only the two disposable test panes

mapped_gui_input.mapping_verification: An OUTPUT_MARKER sent to the exact /bin/cat pane with tmux send-keys appeared in the corresponding iTerm mapped pane screen.

readonly_viewer.input_method: iTerm session connector send_text with a unique marker and newline

writable_control_baseline.input_method: Same iTerm session connector send_text with a unique marker and newline

interpretation: The actual mapped iTerm2 pane did not forward keyboard input to the /bin/cat pane under -CC -r.
The writable -CC baseline forwarded the same type of input, confirming the probe targeted the mapped pane and the input path worked.
The read_only property means native mapped-GUI input is blocked; it does not grant or enforce Control Mode command permissions.
A send-keys command on the same -C -r control-mode channel was accepted and mutated the pane. Coordinator writes must remain on the trusted runtime path and obey its policy.
limitations: This live check used one macOS host, iTerm2, and tmux 3.6a.
It does not verify Terminal.app fallback, Linux GUI behavior, or other tmux releases.
